title: IMS/VoLTE SDP Session-Description Structural Validation and Parser Shielding
description: Synthetic evaluation of whether grammar- and state-aware validation of SIP/IMS session-negotiation messages (Session Description Protocol attributes exchanged during VoLTE/IMS call setup) can reject malformed or out-of-sequence messages before they reach baseband handler code, modeled on a recurring pattern of unvalidated SDP attribute parsing documented across four related baseband CVEs from the same vendor and disclosure batch.

related_cves.trust_boundary: Internet/carrier IMS network to baseband processor (no radio adjacency required)
related_cves.vendor_mitigation: Apply Samsung's March 2023 Semiconductor Security Bulletin OTA fix via the device OEM/carrier update channel; interim workaround (Project Zero recommendation): disable Wi-Fi Calling and VoLTE to remove the reachable SDP-processing path.
related_cves.mitigation_gap: Partial: Samsung shipped an OTA fix (Google Pixel patched in the March 2023 ASPL; other OEMs lagged), but no per-OEM fixed-build mapping or baseband compromise-assessment guidance is published. Scoring note: NVD enrichment lists CVSS 9.8 Critical, while the MITRE/CNA record (following Samsung's own DoS-oriented description) lists 7.5 High - both retained per source rather than resolved to one figure.

failure_pattern: During VoLTE/IMS SIP-based call/session setup, a mobile baseband processor automatically parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes describing the negotiated media session (e.g. accept-type, fmtp, video-configuration, chatroom property count) before any subscriber action. Insufficient length and value validation on individual SDP attributes allows a maliciously crafted session-negotiation message, delivered simply by reaching the victim's phone number over the carrier IMS network, to corrupt baseband memory - in every case without the subscriber answering or interacting with the device.
vendor_mitigation: Samsung shipped an OTA firmware fix via its March 2023 Semiconductor Security Bulletin, delivered through the device OEM/carrier update channel; Google Project Zero additionally recommended disabling Wi-Fi Calling and VoLTE as an interim workaround to remove the reachable SDP-processing path pending the update.
mitigation_gap: Across all four CVEs, Samsung's own bulletin does not publish a per-OEM fixed-build mapping, so a chipset-level fix does not by itself prove an affected handset has received and is running the corrected firmware; no baseband-level compromise-assessment or forensic guidance is published for any of the four records. NVD and MITRE/CNA also disagree on severity scoring for three of the four CVEs (9.8 Critical vs 7.5-8.6 High) - both are recorded per CVE rather than resolved to a single invented figure.
research_question: Can grammar and state-aware validation reject malformed or out-of-sequence SDP/session-description messages before baseband handler execution?
hypothesis: A strict header-normalisation, size-limit, mandatory-field, sequence-validation and state-machine-enforcement layer will reject a materially higher proportion of malformed synthetic SDP/session-negotiation messages than a weak baseline with incomplete mandatory-field and state checks, while preserving acceptance of valid session-setup messages.
